title: Prove the sharp rank cap for three-call A5 conjugate pairs
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof: the A5 conjugate-pair target with orthogonal block ranks r,s has exact paid-call minimum three if h>=r+s, and four if max(r,s)<=h<r+s, over every field and every finite dirty role space. The paid alphabet allows idempotent couplings of rank at most h. After scalar normalization, every three-call word forces its middle coupling to be P+Q. Free scalar mixing does not lower this threshold.

```text
four calls: F_x(P) F_y(P)   F_y(Q) F_x(Q)
three calls: F_x(P) F_y(P+Q)        F_x(Q)
```

Both words have total coupling rank 2(r+s). This saves one call overhead in the changed alphabet; it does not claim a cheaper native implementation or new kappa.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Wentao Li #4089 for the arbitrary-role binary rank-one theorem, support filter and forced middle projector in that special case; Cinna Davis #2246 for the original target, finite theorem and question; and their retained PR840/register-model lineage. Those results are cited, not audited or replayed. The new claim is the higher-rank cap transition, arbitrary-rank construction and field-uniform proof. Predecessor files and credit remain unchanged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review and global literature priority are unclaimed.

## Evidence

- Before: the cited rank-one binary model needs four calls. After changing the cap, the complete three-call word is legal exactly when h>=r+s. The written coefficient argument proves necessity over every field, without a finite-width search assumption.
- The standalone verifier enumerates all 21,952 ternary and 262,144 quinary three-call words in the complete two-role idempotent alphabets, including zero and rank-two couplings. There are 24 and 60 hits across 12 and 30 target pairs; every hit has rank-two middle coupling.
- Further exact evidence: fifteen short label words, 60 full endpoints from 30 oblique pairs over Q/F2/F3/F5/F7, 480 independently evaluated regular-action basis columns, 210 omission controls, six invalid-input controls and one dirty-spectator leakage control.
- CPython 3.12.15/macOS, standard library only. Warning-strict normal and optimized direct runs pass in 6.74 and 6.79 seconds. The registered normal/optimized replay passes in 14.15 seconds total. Each registered command is below the five-minute local target. Generated receipts bind all six package files to SHA256 hashes; no receipt is hand-written.
- Metadata/source pins and AST/function-bound diagnostics pass. Committed-byte/source-history preflight and the official six-file export integrity check pass at 5e39aa59ac51cf965a866e4d0b35119fe5629eb7. Both read-only Git-free empty-PATH export replays pass with identical generated receipts.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem fixes these A5 labels, orthogonal idempotent target blocks, full formal group-algebra equality and h>=max(r,s). It gives no optimum for a smaller cap or arbitrary rank-dependent tariff. Total rank mass is unchanged. Native higher-rank implementation, scalar mixing, movement, frames, preparation, storage, restoration charges, precision, compiler closure and a complete recursive consumer remain unpriced. No supplier admission, selected-frontier change, complete multiplication theorem, selected scientific replay, Lean or Docker run is claimed. The all-field result is the written proof; finite tests are corroboration.

## Open next questions

Can one actual nonabelian native caller execute the combined middle call for less than the two separate y calls? Start with a runtime rank-two idempotent action and give the full scalar-mixing, movement, frame and return invoice on arbitrary dirty data. The missing native tariff and recursive consumer block profitability. No follow-up is reserved.

## Related open work

- #3914 concerns the same A5 alphabet and proves its collapse into an additive caller. The changed rank cap does not remove that obstruction; this package computes no common numerical caller value. Merged #5114/#5186 give distinct carrier/physical rank-one interfaces and are not prices for the enlarged alphabet.

Before DONE, this account's ten open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-27T10:05:55Z were refreshed: #5865 through #5874. The other nine result descriptions concern different objects or quantities; none studies this A5 conjugate-pair paid-rank threshold. No common computed value or numerical disagreement was identified. No additional mathematical computation was run to check those contributions.
